description: The bar chart illustrates the evaluation matches between a large language model (LLM) judge and human annotations across six distinct categories—“No Hallucination,” “Oriented,” “Active,” “Self-aware,” “Rigorous,” and “Correct”—based on 300 annotated samples. The horizontal axis represents percentage values ranging from 0% to 100%, with tick marks at 20% intervals, while the vertical axis lists the six evaluation categories in descending order of “Matched” percentage. Each category is represented by a horizontal stacked bar, divided into two segments: a dominant dark blue portion labeled “Matched,” indicating the percentage of agreement between the LLM and human annotators, and a smaller light blue portion labeled “Not Matched,” representing disagreement. The “Matched” percentages are explicitly labeled on each bar: 98.33% for “No Hallucination,” 97.33% for “Oriented,” 97.00% for “Active,” 94.00% for “Self-aware,” 95.33% for “Rigorous,” and 99.00% for “Correct.” The corresponding “Not Matched” percentages are also labeled: 1.67%, 2.67%, 3.00%, 6.00%, 4.67%, and 1.00%, respectively. The chart visually emphasizes high alignment between the LLM and human judgments, with “Correct” showing the highest agreement (99.00%) and “Self-aware” the lowest (94.00%). The legend in the center-right clarifies the color coding: dark blue for “Matched” and light blue for “Not Matched.”
